sections.subtitle: Only disclosed for FY2023 and FY2025 in the filings parsed so far — the board announced in April 2026 that Primark (Retail) will demerge from the four Food segments (Grocery, Sugar, Agriculture, Ingredients) by end-2027

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Associated British Foods plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Associated British Foods plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Associated British Foods plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Associated British Foods plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Associated British Foods plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Associated British Foods plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Associated British Foods plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Associated British Foods plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
ABF reports five segments: Grocery (Twinings, Ovaltine, Patak's, Allied Bakeries), Sugar, Agriculture, Ingredients (AB Mauri, SPI Pharma) and Retail (Primark). Only FY2023 and FY2025 are broken out in the filings parsed so far.

For Associated British Foods plc: in April 2026 the board decided to demerge Primark (Retail) from the other four segments (together "FoodCo"), targeting completion by end of calendar 2027. Retail alone (£9.5bn FY2025) is now bigger than the other four segments combined (£9.97bn), so the split approximates the two post-demerger entities.

What to watch:

  • Whether Retail keeps growing faster than the Food segments, widening the size gap between the two future companies
  • Sugar's swing to a loss-making adjusted operating profit in FY2025 — the segment most exposed to commodity price cycles
  • Separation costs (~£75m one-off) and dis-synergies (~£45m/yr) once they start appearing against these lines

segmentProfit.title: Segment adjusted operating profit
segmentProfit.content:
Adjusted operating profit by the same five segments, before significant items. This is the profitability lens the demerger separates: Primark (Retail) versus the FoodCo segments (Grocery, Sugar, Agriculture, Ingredients).

For Associated British Foods plc: Retail's adjusted operating profit grew from £735m (FY2023) to £1,126m (FY2025) while Sugar flipped from a £169m profit to a £42m loss over the same two years — Primark is carrying a disproportionate and growing share of group profit ahead of the split.

What to watch:

  • Grocery and Ingredients margins, the steadier of the four Food segments
  • Whether Sugar returns to profit before the demerger completes
  • Each segment's profit as a standalone base for valuing Primark and FoodCo separately once they trade apart

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Associated British Foods plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Associated British Foods plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
